full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff is, in brief, that the former Jaminder Moharaja Shashikanto Acharya Chowdhury was the owner of the suit land under whom Ram Sundar Dutta was tenant. Ram Sunder Dutta died leaving behind two sons, namely Satish Chandra Dutta and Romesh Chandra Dutta. Satish Chandra Dutta and Ram Chandra Dutta settled the suit land with Jan Mahmud Sheikh, Enam Box Bepari and Mirajuddin Sheikh. The CS Khatian was prepared accordingly. Out of the suit land, the land of plot No. 1073 was recorded in the name of Jan Mahmud and the land of plot Nos. 1070 and 1975 were recorded in the names of Enam Box Bepari and Mirajuddin. Jan Mahmud surrendered his land to the landlord. Thereafter, the plaintiff's father took settlement of the said land from the landlords, since such settlement he had been enjoying and possessing the same by paying rent to the landlords. While the said landlords expressed their wish to sell the suit property, the father of the plaintiff expressed his interest to purchase that land, but ultimately the land was not sold to them. The father of the plaintiff converted the suit land into a pond and had been enjoying and possessing the pond by rearing fishes therein. By operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 plaintiff's father acquired title in the suit land. During settlement survey the government officials assured him that the suit land would be recorded properly in his name in the SA Khatian. His father transferred the suit land to the plaintiff by way of oral gift and since then he has been enjoying and possessing the same. With an intention to mortgage the suit land with the bank to get loan he went to the local Tahshil office wherefrom he came to know the suit land was recorded as khas property of the government though he has been enjoying and possessing the same, and hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant-government contested the suit by filing written statement denying the claims of the plaintiff stating that the suit land has been properly recorded as Government's khas land and the plaintiff has got no right, title and possession over the suit land. 

 8. To oppose his such argument, Mr Abdul Hoque, the learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite party, submits that the Review Case itself is not maintainable and the learned Joint District Judge, without any cause for review illegally entertained the application for review, which occasioned failure of justice and for ends of justice the Review Case itself is liable to be rejected. In support of his such contention he cited the decisions in the cases of Md Shafique Ahmed vs Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs reported in 11 MLR (AD) 174, Mia Lutfi Khasru vs Bangladesh reported in 55 DLR (AD) 74 and Nurul Hussain vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 49 DLR (AD) 108.
